# flowrap

> A wrapper-first board for Svelte 5: zoom, pan, node dragging, edges, and
> links you draw with the mouse. You wrap YOUR existing component and get a
> position, a drag gesture and ports — with no "node types" to register and no
> data schema to declare up front.

This file is the complete public API reference in one self-contained document.
It matches the installed version of the package.

- Requires `svelte@^5` (peer dependency).
- Install: `npm i flowrap`
- There is NO separate CSS file to import: the styles live in the components'
  own `<style>` blocks.

## ⚠️ Two things that break everything if you don't know them

**1. The element around `<FlowBoard>` must have a non-zero height.**
`.fr-viewport` is declared as `height: 100%`, so the height comes from the
consumer. Without it the board collapses to zero: no nodes visible, no dragging,
everything looks broken. This is the single most common first problem.

```svelte
<div><FlowBoard>…</FlowBoard></div>                       <!-- EMPTY -->
<div style="height: 70vh"><FlowBoard>…</FlowBoard></div>  <!-- correct -->
```

**2. The library does not own the graph and does not create edges.**
A mouse drag ends by calling `onconnect` with a description of the connection —
that's all. Putting the link into your own array, sending it to a server, or
rejecting it is the consumer's decision. Deletion works the same way: remove the
item from your array and the `<FlowEdge>` disappears. There is no
`board.addEdge()` method and there will not be one.

## Exports

Exactly six, plus types:

```ts
import {
  FlowBoard,    // the board: zoom, pan, the SVG layer for edges
  FlowNode,     // wrapper around your markup: position + drag
  FlowEdge,     // a link between nodes (headless, renders nothing itself)
  FlowHandle,   // a port you drag a link from
  screenToFlow, // screen → world
  flowToScreen  // world → screen
} from 'flowrap';

import type {
  Position,     // { x: number; y: number }
  Viewport,     // { pan: Position; zoom: number }
  Connection,   // { from, to, fromHandle?, toHandle? } — what onconnect gives you
  EdgePathType, // 'straight' | 'bezier' | 'step'
  HandleType    // 'source' | 'target' | 'both'
} from 'flowrap';
```

## `<FlowBoard>`

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zoom` | `number` | `1` | `$bindable` |
| `pan` | `Position` | `{ x: 0, y: 0 }` | `$bindable` |
| `positions` | `Record<string, Position>` | `{}` | `$bindable`, snapshot of the whole board |
| `minZoom` | `number` | `0.1` | |
| `maxZoom` | `number` | `4` | |
| `zoomSpeed` | `number` | `0.002` | `zoom * Math.exp(-deltaY * zoomSpeed)` |
| `onconnect` | `(c: Connection) => void` | — | a drag ended on a valid drop |
| `isValidConnection` | `(c: Connection) => boolean` | — | your own connection policy |

Dragging the background pans the board; the wheel zooms towards the cursor. A
drag that starts on a node or a port does not pan the board.

## `<FlowNode>`

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | — | required, unique within the board |
| `x` | `number` | `0` | `$bindable` |
| `y` | `number` | `0` | `$bindable` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | disables dragging |

The wrapper gets a `data-fr-node={id}` attribute — that's what tests and styles
target. It must be rendered inside `<FlowBoard>`, otherwise it throws.

There is no controlled/uncontrolled flag — `bind:` decides:

```svelte
<FlowNode id="a" x={40} y={40}>…</FlowNode>   <!-- the node keeps its position -->
<FlowNode id="a" bind:x bind:y>…</FlowNode>   <!-- the parent owns the position -->
```

## `<FlowEdge>`

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | `string` | — | source node id |
| `to` | `string` | — | target node id |
| `type` | `'bezier' \| 'straight' \| 'step'` | `'bezier'` | line shape |
| `id` | `string` | `$props.id()` | registry key |
| `fromHandle` | `string` | — | port id on the `from` end |
| `toHandle` | `string` | — | port id on the `to` end |

Declared inside `<FlowBoard>`, next to the nodes. It **renders nothing itself**:
it registers with the board's context, and one shared SVG layer draws the lines —
beneath the nodes and with `pointer-events: none`, so it never intercepts panning
or dragging. An edge with an unknown `from`/`to` is silently not drawn. Two edges
between the same pair of nodes do not collapse into one.

## `<FlowHandle>`

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | — | unique WITHIN ITS OWN node |
| `type` | `'source' \| 'target' \| 'both'` | `'both'` | direction |

Declared **inside the node's content**; it finds its node through context, so
there is no `node` prop to pass. Any other attributes (`class`, `aria-*`,
`data-*`) are forwarded to the port element. Where the port ends up is decided by
your layout, not by a library schema: there is no `handles: [{ position:
'right' }]`.

## Recipes

### A minimal board with your own component

```svelte
<script>
  import { FlowBoard, FlowNode } from 'flowrap';
  import MyCard from './MyCard.svelte';
</script>

<div style="height: 70vh">
  <FlowBoard>
    <FlowNode id="a" x={40} y={40}><MyCard title="A" /></FlowNode>
    <FlowNode id="b" x={320} y={200}><MyCard title="B" /></FlowNode>
  </FlowBoard>
</div>
```

### Links: creating by dragging, and deleting

```svelte
<script>
  import { FlowBoard, FlowNode, FlowEdge, FlowHandle } from 'flowrap';

  let links = $state([]);

  // The library does NOT create the edge — it only reports the drop.
  const add = (c) => (links = [...links, { id: crypto.randomUUID(), ...c }]);
  // Deleting is on your side too: drop it from the array and the edge is gone.
  const remove = (id) => (links = links.filter((l) => l.id !== id));
</script>

<div style="height: 70vh">
  <FlowBoard onconnect={add}>
    <FlowNode id="a" x={40} y={40}>
      <div class="card">A <FlowHandle id="out" type="source" /></div>
    </FlowNode>
    <FlowNode id="b" x={320} y={200}>
      <div class="card"><FlowHandle id="in" type="target" /> B</div>
    </FlowNode>

    {#each links as link (link.id)}
      <FlowEdge from={link.from} to={link.to}
                fromHandle={link.fromHandle} toHandle={link.toHandle} />
    {/each}
  </FlowBoard>
</div>

<ul>
  {#each links as link (link.id)}
    <li>{link.from} → {link.to}
      <button onclick={() => remove(link.id)}>delete</button>
    </li>
  {/each}
</ul>
```

In TypeScript, type the array explicitly — `Connection` has optional handles, so
inferring the type from a seed array with required ones makes the spread in
`onconnect` fail to type-check:

```ts
import type { Connection } from 'flowrap';

type Link = Connection & { id: string };
let links = $state<Link[]>([]);
```

### Validating connections

Before `onconnect` fires, a link passes three checks in this order: self-connect
is rejected → port directions must be compatible → your `isValidConnection`. If
any of them fails, the preview line disappears and `onconnect` is not called.

```svelte
<FlowBoard
  isValidConnection={(c) => !links.some((l) => l.from === c.from && l.to === c.to)}
  onconnect={add}
/>
```

### Saving and restoring a layout

```svelte
<script>
  let positions = $state({});
  const save = () => localStorage.setItem('layout', JSON.stringify(positions));
  const load = () => {
    const raw = localStorage.getItem('layout');
    if (raw) positions = JSON.parse(raw); // the nodes really do move
  };
</script>

<FlowBoard bind:positions>…</FlowBoard>
```

Works both ways. While a node is being dragged, incoming assignments for that
node are ignored. `bind:x`/`bind:y` and `bind:positions` can be used together;
assigning to both slices in the same tick is not supported.

### Ports on all four sides of a card

Positioning is yours — the library only supplies the dot and the gesture. The
card needs `position: relative`.

```svelte
<FlowNode id="a">
  <div class="card">
    <FlowHandle id="n" class="n" />
    <FlowHandle id="e" class="e" />
  </div>
</FlowNode>

<style>
  .card { position: relative; padding: 16px; }
  .card :global(.n) { position: absolute; top: -5px;  left: 50%; }
  .card :global(.e) { position: absolute; right: -5px; top: 50%; }
</style>
```

### Appearance

```css
.my-board {
  --fr-edge-stroke: #999;
  --fr-edge-width: 1.5;

  --fr-handle-size: 10px;
  --fr-handle-bg: #fff;
  --fr-handle-border: #666;

  --fr-connection-stroke: #4a9eff;  /* the preview line while dragging */
  --fr-connection-width: 2;
  --fr-connection-dash: 4 4;
}
```

Selectors: `.fr-viewport`, `.fr-world`, `.fr-edges`, `.fr-edge`,
`.fr-connection`, `.fr-handle`, `[data-fr-node]`, `[data-fr-handle]`.

### Coordinate helpers

```ts
screenToFlow({ x, y }, { pan, zoom }); // screen → world
flowToScreen({ x, y }, { pan, zoom }); // world → screen
```

Both work in coordinates **local to `.fr-viewport`** (the board's top-left corner
is `{0,0}`), not page coordinates. Convert from `clientX/clientY` yourself:

```ts
const rect = viewportEl.getBoundingClientRect();
const local = { x: e.clientX - rect.left, y: e.clientY - rect.top };
```

## What flowrap does NOT have

Read this section. By analogy with react-flow / svelte-flow it is easy to write
an API that does not exist here.

- There is no `<MiniMap>`, `<Controls>` or `<Background>` — those components
  don't exist.
- There is no `nodes={[]}` / `edges={[]}` prop and no `nodeTypes` registration.
  Nodes and edges are declared as markup; the graph state is yours.
- There is no `onEdgeClick`, `onNodeClick`, `deletable`, `selectable`,
  `board.addEdge()` or `board.deleteEdge()`.
- **No deleting edges with the mouse and no edge selection.** The edge layer has
  `pointer-events: none` — without it, panning breaks. Deletion goes through
  your own array (see the recipe above).
- **No reconnect** — you cannot drag the end of an existing edge onto another
  port.
- No multi-select and no creating several links in one gesture.
- No arrowheads or markers on edge ends, and no labels on edges.
- No orthogonal routing around nodes: `type="step"` gives an orthogonal line but
  does not avoid obstacles.
- No highlighting of compatible ports during a drag.
- No magnet to a port across empty space: a drop on the card's body lands on the
  nearest compatible port OF THAT node, but nothing is attracted through empty
  space.
- Self-edges (`from === to`) are not supported: the path degenerates to a point.

## Gotchas

- **A parent with no height** — see the top of this file.
- **Nodes with no `x`/`y` all sit at `(0,0)`**, and the last one in the DOM
  intercepts `pointerdown` from the rest. Spread them out with coordinates.
- **A port is declared inside the node's content**, not next to it. A port
  outside `<FlowNode>` throws a clear error.
- **A port moved without a size change** (reordering inside a flex container,
  changing `order`) does not recompute its geometry: measurement runs through a
  `ResizeObserver` on the port itself and on its `offsetParent`. The workaround
  is to change something observable, e.g. the card's size.
- **SSR/prerender emits the first HTML without lines** — there is no DOM on the
  server, so node sizes cannot be measured. The lines appear on hydration.
